profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at an academic-industry ML research lab about an existing proposal to reproduce and evaluate ZORB for inclusion in the lab's internal 'fast-training methods' benchmark report. The proposal already specifies a replication of the paper's headline MNIST result and a smaller CIFAR-10 follow-up, and the meeting is meant to judge whether the evaluation design is sufficiently sound to approve engineering time and compute budget. The agenda is to review the proposed timing protocol, baseline setup, and model implementation plan, then decide whether the proposal is ready to move from design into execution. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on the current evaluation plan plus a short list of implementation next steps.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: optimization methods, empirical benchmarking, reproducibility studies
members.background: Lena leads small-scale evaluations of unconventional training algorithms and often turns flashy papers into internal benchmark notes for the lab's model efficiency program.
members.private_state: She wants the review to approve a lean replication plan quickly so the team can test whether ZORB is worth a workshop note before the quarter ends, and she is trying to avoid expanding the scope into a full infrastructure-heavy benchmark effort.
hidden_assumptions: A speed claim is still fairly represented if one-time algorithm-specific setup costs, such as pseudoinverse preparation, are treated as initialization rather than part of training time.
Using the lab's previously selected Adam benchmark preset still counts as 'without hyperparameter tuning' as long as no new sweep is run for this project.
The binding reference for the MNIST experiment is the paper's appendix architecture, even if the lab already has a similarly named template in the benchmark repository.
For this design review, reproducing the headline MNIST result is enough to justify moving forward; broader packaging and robustness checks can come later.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.role: Senior ML Systems Engineer, Benchmarking Infrastructure
members.expertise: training pipelines, experiment harnesses, timing instrumentation, reproducible evaluation
members.background: Omar maintains the lab's benchmarking stack and is responsible for making new methods fit the shared dashboard, timing conventions, and reusable model templates.
members.private_state: He wants any approved plan to fit smoothly into the existing benchmark harness so his team does not end up supporting a one-off evaluation pipeline that produces incomparable numbers.
hidden_assumptions: A benchmark speedup number should mean end-to-end wall-clock time as recorded by the standard harness, including startup and method-specific setup overhead.
If a paper says 'without hyperparameter tuning,' the clean baseline interpretation is to use a single default Adam configuration rather than a preset that was historically chosen after sweeps.
When a proposal mentions the '11-layer MNIST model,' the safest implementation is the repository's existing mnist_mlp_11 template unless someone explicitly replaces it line by line.
If this review approves the design, the runs are expected to be generated through the normal dashboard pipeline rather than a custom timing script.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts toward the reported speedup
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'reproduce the 300x speedup' and talk about 'training time' as if it were a single obvious quantity.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means time spent in the iterative optimization portion up to a comparable convergence point, treating ZORB's one-time pseudoinverse-related setup as initialization that does not belong in the headline speed claim.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means end-to-end wall-clock time from job start to reported result as logged by the benchmark harness, including startup overhead, pseudoinverse setup, checkpointing, and other method-specific costs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML papers and internal dashboards, 'training time' is routinely used without a timing protocol being restated, so both participants hear a familiar phrase and assume the other is using the locally obvious convention.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'without hyperparameter tuning' permits for the Adam baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both endorse preserving the paper's 'without hyperparameter tuning' framing for the comparison against Adam.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that the lab's standard Adam preset from an earlier benchmark effort is acceptable because no new tuning will be done specifically for ZORB.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that 'without hyperparameter tuning' means a literal default Adam configuration in a single run, not a preset that was historically chosen after prior sweeps.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither person experiences their interpretation as a choice being made now; each treats it as pre-set context attached to the phrase 'no tuning,' so the disagreement hides inside background assumptions rather than explicit planning.

misalignment_points.topic: Which exact '11-layer MNIST model' is being implemented
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the 11-layer MNIST model' and 'the paper architecture' as though those phrases identify one unambiguous object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the architecture described in the ZORB manuscript appendix: a plain feed-forward network with the paper's specific hidden-width pattern and no normalization or dropout.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the lab's existing repository template called mnist_mlp_11, whose internal layer-count convention differs and which keeps LayerNorm and dropout enabled unless explicitly removed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The names overlap enough that both feel they are referencing the same experiment, and because the meeting is a design review rather than an implementation walkthrough, neither expects the shorthand to conceal a materially different instantiated model.
